title: Identity Preservation Test
purpose: Test whether a stable B32K symbolic identity surface helps preserve conceptual identity across LLM interpretation compared with prose-only and decorative-metadata baselines.

symbols.name: decorative_context
symbols.definition: Extra text, labels, metadata, summaries, or framing that may improve readability but does not necessarily constrain inference.

symbols.name: constraint_bearing_context
symbols.definition: Context that restricts or guides interpretation by binding concepts to roles, boundaries, dependencies, recurrence paths, or coherence requirements.

symbols.name: shared_cell_recurrence
symbols.definition: A recurrent contextual grouping in which local units share constraint-bearing structure across repeated roles or cells.

symbols.name: frontier_exposure
symbols.definition: Exposure to boundary, edge, hard-case, or transition regions where coherence failure becomes easier to detect.

symbols.name: tail_exposure
symbols.definition: Exposure to low-frequency, peripheral, or non-central cases that test whether structure survives away from easy central examples.

symbols.name: mixed_role_organization
symbols.definition: A contextual organization in which elements participate in multiple functional roles rather than appearing as flat isolated facts.

symbols.name: global_coherence_failure
symbols.definition: A failure of consistency across the whole structure, even when local views appear plausible.

symbols.name: local_mimicry
symbols.definition: The ability to imitate a local pattern or shell profile without preserving global structure.

symbols.name: shuffle_null_survival
symbols.definition: Persistence of a signal after comparison against shuffled controls, suggesting that organization matters beyond raw content volume.

symbols.name: trusted_symbolic_surface
symbols.definition: A stable symbolic identity layer that preserves named conceptual objects before interpretation begins.

relations.name: contrasts_with
relations.definition: Marks two identities as importantly different and not interchangeable.

relations.name: supports
relations.definition: Marks one identity as providing support for another.

relations.name: exposes
relations.definition: Marks one identity as making another identity visible or testable.

relations.name: tests
relations.definition: Marks one identity as a pressure condition for another.

relations.name: preserves_identity_of
relations.definition: Marks a structure as helping maintain the identity of another structure across interpretation.

claims.name: decorative_context_may_not_constrain_inference
claims.text: Decorative context may add readability or metadata without actually constraining the inference path.

claims.name: shared_cell_recurrence_can_create_nontrivial_signal
claims.text: Shared-cell recurrence may create a nontrivial signal because it organizes local units through repeated constraint-bearing context.

claims.name: frontier_exposure_marks_boundary_cases
claims.text: Frontier exposure marks hard or boundary cases where global coherence failure can become more visible.

claims.name: global_coherence_failure_is_not_local_pattern_failure
claims.text: Global coherence failure is not the same as local pattern failure; a local view can mimic the target while the whole structure fails.

claims.name: trusted_surface_is_identity_layer_not_meaning_itself
claims.text: A trusted symbolic surface preserves identity but does not define meaning by itself.

test_questions: Explain the difference between decorative context and constraint-bearing context.
Give an example where local mimicry succeeds but global coherence fails.
Explain why frontier exposure might reveal coherence failure.
Is a trusted symbolic surface the same thing as meaning? Answer carefully.
Which concepts should not be collapsed into each other?
